page: UpCloud 48xCPU-256GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.33 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 2048 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-threaded performance. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. However, multi-threaded capabilities are robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 25% and passmark CPU encryption testing also reaching the top 25%. General multi-core metrics, such as Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, sit in the middle 50% average tier.

The primary tradeoff of this instance lies in its shared CPU allocation and low single-core clock speed of 2.0 GHz, which limits its suitability for single-threaded tasks. However, the high resource density of 48 physical cores and 256 GB of RAM provides qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can distribute execution across many cores. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform consistently in the average tier, making it a stable platform for multi-threaded applications.

This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, parallel data processing, static web serving, and database operations. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks for smaller models, though text generation speeds drop significantly for larger models.
